sections.overview: Platystomatichthys sturio is a freshwater pimelodid catfish native to the Amazon basin.
sections.identification: Its common name refers to its sturgeon-like head and body profile; despite the resemblance, it is a catfish, not a sturgeon.
sections.habitat: It is a demersal species reported from tropical freshwater in the Amazon basin.
sections.diet: The references consulted do not provide a reliable, detailed description of its wild diet.
sections.behavior: Species-specific activity and social behavior are not well documented in the sources consulted.
sections.reproduction: Breeding biology is not detailed in the references consulted.
sections.ecology: Much of its natural history remains unresolved in the available species accounts.
sections.conservation: The IUCN assessment published in 2023 lists it as Least Concern, while noting that information about the species is limited.
